questionText:

"Ibn Battuta was fascinated by plants that were completely unfamiliar to his North African audience. Describing the coconut, he wrote: 'These trees are among the most peculiar trees in the world... The nut of a coconut tree resembles a human head, for in it are what look like two eyes and a mouth, and inside, when it is green, there is what looks like brains, and within it which is like hair. They make from this cordage with which they sew up ships instead of iron nails.' Describing the betel (paan), he noted: 'The betel is a tree which is cultivated in the same manner as the grape-vine... The betel has no fruit and is grown only for the sake of its leaves... The manner of its use is that before eating it one takes the areca nut, which is like a nutmeg, breaks it into small pellets and puts these in his mouth and chews them.
